title: The moment you change an area to process mode disabled, body_exited signal will be emited
body: ### Tested versions Godot 4.4 Stable ### System information Windows 10 Godot 4.4 stable ### Issue description I can understand this happening when changing a body to process mode disabled, and then an active overlaping area emits body_exited. This happens too and maybe it makes sense. What I don't understand is the opposite. If i'm disabling the area is because I dont' want it to do anything. Why it emits the signal? Is this inteded? Is this a bug? I'm not sure, but in my specific issue it's a big problem I don't know how to solve. Basically I just need to pause a complex scene I have loaded separatly at the same time an active scene is running. I want to tuly pause it. I don't want anything happening after pausing it. Checked and it also happens in 2d btw ### Steps to reproduce Create a 3d scene, add an area and a characterbody3d with any default collisions. Make sure they overlap. Add this script to the main 3d scene: ``` extends Node3D @onready var character_body_3d: CharacterBody3D = $CharacterBody3D func _ready() -> void: print("start") await get_tree().create_timer(1).timeout process_mode=Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED func _on_area_3d_body_exited(body: Node3D) -> void: print(body.name," exited") ``` body_exit will be called after 1 second. It happens even if you change the mode to the body or area specifically instead of the entire scene (at first I though it was a tree propagation order thing). ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21327881/test.zip)
